items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And so he put on a concert called “Four Generations of Jazz Cornet” and I was the young generation, there was a guy from Boston named Paul Monnet, who was maybe in his thirties at the time

ctx.x: Have you been able to kind of play alongside some of your influences or heroes?

Yeah. That’s a good one. Yeah, I was very fortunate. Aside from meeting the local heroes around Detroit and playing with some of them, which were probably mostly names you might not know but it was a thrill, every year I’d get to play with better and better musicians. One of the first ones I got to play with was a guy named Tom Saunders in Detroit, who is a very great cornet player and I used to go and hear him when I wasn’t even really old enough to be in the bars that he was playing in, but we’d go and hear…

concert, which was a shock. He was going to be 72 I believe. We had played with him two nights before, and he was in great shape and full of energy and playing great, no signs of any health problems. He just all of a sudden had a heart attack and that was it. And I’ll never forget how well Dizzy Gillespie handled this. We did the concert with one of J.C.’s proteges, a guy named Billy Cairo, a drummer in Detroit, and Dizzy managed to pay tribute to J.C., his old friend, really nicely, but also make it a happy…
